messages:
Alex K: Heads up — cost dashboard shows ~0.7% of requests with no billing_key after sampling. Repro: 1) sample 10% at edge, 2) proxy dedupe + compact batching, 3) ingest shows envelope.root.billing_key missing. Anyone seen this?
Maya P: Hmm. Which path is doing the compacting? edge-proxy or ingest pre-processor?
Alex K: Looks like the proxy does an early dedupe then we run compactEnvelope() in ingest. Example headers we receive: `X-Billing-Key: tenant_42|policyA` then later envelope has null. Logs: `received headers {req_id: r123, billing_key: tenant_42}` -> `post-compact envelope.root.billing_key = null`
Frank H: I dug into the compacting code last week. compactEnvelope() currently prefers the first seen attribute set and drops duplicates when merging spans. If sampling + reorder happens the billing_key can be lost if it was present only on a sampled span that got dropped.
Liam S: Root cause sounds like attribute loss during span merge + sampling. Options: 1) push billing_key into the envelope root earlier (pre-enrich at edge), 2) stash billing_key in a small pre-enrich store that survives sampling, 3) do an async billing-key lookup at ingest (backfill). Tradeoffs: #1 avoids lookups but increases edge writes/cardinality; #3 is cheaper but produces delayed/possibly wrong attribution.
Maya P: Backfill worries me — late attribution could break per-route SLOs that trigger budget rules. We need either synchronous presence or a confidence flag in metrics.
Alex K: Agreed. Also worried about cost: if we push root keys at edge we increase index cardinality for envelopes (more unique keys). But probably better accuracy.
Frank H: What about a hybrid? For high-QPS routes (model-serving) do pre-enrich root billing_key; for low-QPS routes rely on backfill with a TTL-based cache. We can gate with config: `preenrich.routes = ["/v1/generate"]`.
Liam S: Hybrid seems pragmatic. Also propose we set an "approx_billing" tag when backfill used, with confidence scores (0.7/1.0). That keeps analytics honest and avoids silent misbilling.
ingest-bot: sampling-rate: 10% | ingest-compact-version: v2 | alert: sampling-reorder-ratio=0.012
Maya P: OK — action items: 1) Alex — spin up a 1% canary with pre-enrich root injection for /v1/generate, 2) Frank — add approx_billing flag in ingest pipeline + metrics, 3) Liam — write short eval for cost/cardinality impact. Can we aim for a follow-up RFC?
Frank H: I'll add the approx_billing tag and a counter metric `ingest.billing_key_missing` so we can measure before/after.
Liam S: I'll run a quick sketch: expected cardinality delta + estimated storage cost (S3 + index) for tenant key at root. 24h experiment should give signal.
Alex K: I'll deploy canary tomorrow and share logs. Putting a draft ticket: https://rwd/issue/INF-8023
Maya P: Perfect. After the 24h canary we reconvene — if missing rate drops to <0.05% we roll. If not, escalate to design RFC with perf numbers. :thumbsup:
Alex K: thanks — will update thread with canary link
Frank H: ack :shipit:
